notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.
Silo is the level where the clock, not the guards, is the real opponent: it runs on a hard timer, so route efficiency outranks caution.

nuance.claim: The level runs on a hard timer of roughly eight and a half minutes, so objectives are collected along one forward route rather than by backtracking.
The level is a sequence of fuel rooms and every objective item is inside one of them, so the fuel room order is the route and no objective needs a detour.
The bomb objective is completed by throwing plastique at the paired canisters in each fuel room, not by shooting them.
The satellite has to be photographed intact; stray fire on entering its room can destroy the objective before it is taken.
The satellite objective is completed with the watch camera equipped and fired at the satellite.
The telemetric data is dropped by a scientist rather than sitting as a placed pickup, so it appears only after that scientist is dealt with.
Dropped keycards and data can lodge inside scenery; shooting the item knocks it loose rather than destroying it.
The satellite circuitry is several separate boards spread across different rooms, so the objective is not complete when the first one is taken.
Scientists carry the keycards that open the next room, so progress requires engaging them even though the casualty objective discourages it.
The final corridor is held by Ourumov with soldiers on the stairs; the soldiers are cleared first so the confrontation is not fought from two sides.
Body armour sits on a catwalk in the later part of the level, positioned just before the heaviest fighting, so it is worth the short detour it costs.
Soldiers and scientists share every fuel room, so grenades and explosives thrown into a room usually cost the casualty objective.
